title: Design of a TPS re-entry experiment with active cooled sharp edge and its integration into the vehicle structure.
author: Mariana de Sousa Silva
abstract: Resulting from a cooperation between the Brazilian Space Agency (AEB - Agęncia Espacial Brasileira) and the German Aerospace Center (DLR - Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt), the SARA project (Satellite for Re-entry in the Atmosphere) aims the development of a recoverable orbital platform for microgravity experiments. Being recoverable demands studies and development of a cooling system, such that the capsule is able to withstand the high temperatures of the re-entry process, especially on the nose region. This present work studies the cooling process known as "transpiration cooling" to be employed at this region, constructed with ceramic matrix composites (CMC). Within the scope of this work, an intensive heat transfer analysis has been developed. The analysis procedure was programmed in MatLab® with the possibility to simulate problems with both different boundary conditions as different material and coolant properties. For the SHEFEX experiment, a transpiration cooling analysis based on flat plate assumptions was carried out. Based on a transpiration area of 0.044 m2 and flow conditions of Mach 7.5, Pinfinito = 204.55 Pa , height 42.6 km and heat flux of 500 kW/m2, it was found out that nitrogen mass flow of 1.79 g/s cool down the surface temperature to the tolerable 1500 K. Further investigations demand experimental verification, hence an experimental transpiration cooling setup was designed.
